headline: 76 contracts catalogued across Plume Mainnet, Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Solana: 9 shared protocol contracts (multi-chain), 11 vault share tokens, 34 NestVault entrypoints, 8 Solana cross-chain composer contracts (EVM side), and core Plume chain tokens; RolesAuthority, NestShareSeizer, and NestRedeemOperator identified as key control-surface contracts.

findings.text: D1: Block-explorer name-tag search not directly executed on Plume explorer (explorer.plume.org) or Etherscan due to fetch-call constraints; addresses were instead sourced from the official docs deployment page (D2), which itself references Plume explorer and Etherscan view links for each address. Etherscan search result returned a PLUME token address (0x264145591C080453d7D348F2e04491eeF640Ca5D) unrelated to vaults. No additional addresses surfaced via name-tag search beyond D2 results.

D2: Official deployed-contracts page fetched at https://app.plume.org/docs/developers/smart-contracts. Listed 9 shared EVM contracts (NestVaultPredicateProxy, NestCCTPRelayer, RolesAuthority, NestShareSeizer, NestRedeemOperator, OperatorRegistry, NestAdapter, NestBundler, NestUnlooper) deployed on Plume/Ethereum/BNB Chain; 11 vault share tokens + 34 NestVault entrypoints across 11 vaults (nTBILL, nALPHA, nBASIS, nOPAL, nCREDIT, nWISDOM, nACRDX, nLCRD, nFXCF, nCLOA, nAXI); and 8 Solana OFT composer EVM-side addresses. Data loaded timestamp in page: 2026-09-01T09:18:44.348Z.

D3: Two SlowMist audit PDFs confirmed at https://github.com/plumenetwork/contracts/blob/main/staking/audit/slowmist.pdf and slowmist2.pdf; GitHub rendered HTML pages returned (PDF binary not fetched). Immunefi Attackathon page references a Trail of Bits audit covering Gov token, Smart Wallet, RWA token, and RWA yield token. No in-scope contract addresses extracted from audit scope tables (PDF binary not parsed). Addresses recorded from D2 instead.

D4: GitHub repo github.com/plumenetwork/contracts confirmed public with folders: arc, foundry-template, misc, plume, smart-wallets, staking. No deployment artifacts (broadcast/, hardhat-deploy/, addresses.json) fetched in this run due to tool-call budget constraints; deployed addresses sourced from official docs (D2) rather than repo files. Repo HEAD commit SHA not pinned (fetch returned rendered HTML without SHA in body).

D5: Multi-chain enumeration completed via D2 docs page. Plume Mainnet: all 9 shared + 34 NestVault + 11 share token contracts. Ethereum: NestVaultPredicateProxy, RolesAuthority, NestShareSeizer, NestRedeemOperator, OperatorRegistry, plus vault-specific share tokens and USDC NestVaults for 11 vaults. BNB Chain: NestVaultPredicateProxy, RolesAuthority, NestShareSeizer, NestRedeemOperator, OperatorRegistry, plus USDT NestVaults for nTBILL, nALPHA, nBASIS, nOPAL, nCREDIT, nWISDOM, nACRDX. Solana: 8 OFT mint + 8 OFT store accounts (Solana pubkeys) + 8 EVM-side Plume composer addresses for nTBILL, nALPHA, nBASIS, nOPAL, nWISDOM, nLCRD, nFXCF, nCLOA. Note: protocol.chains lists 'Plume Mainnet, Ethereum, Solana' but BNB Chain deployments also found; search result (cryptobriefing.com) also mentions Avalanche. Avalanche not confirmed from fetched docs.

D6: No factory contract surfaced in docs or GitHub in this run. Vaults appear to be individually deployed rather than factory-spawned per the architecture description (each issuer gets its own segregated vault). No factory enumeration performed.

D7: Role taxonomy applied: RolesAuthority → admin/guardian role; NestShareSeizer → guardian (ability to seize shares); NestRedeemOperator → admin (manages redemption execution); OperatorRegistry → admin (registry); NestVaultPredicateProxy → other (compliance entrypoint); NestCCTPRelayer → other (cross-chain); NestAdapter/Bundler/Unlooper → other (peripheral); share tokens → token; NestVault contracts → vault; Solana OFT composers → other (cross-chain bridge). Actor classes all unknown pending on-chain reads.

D8: All addresses in admin_addresses[] trace to the fetched https://app.plume.org/docs/developers/smart-contracts page. Plume chain token addresses (pUSD 0xdddD73F5Df1F0DC31373357beAC77545dC5A6f3F, WPLUME 0xEa237441c92CAe6FC17Caaf9a7acB3f953be4bd1, USDC 0x222365EF19F7947e5484218551B56bb3965Aa7aF) trace to docs.plume.org/plume/developers/contract-addresses. No snippet-only sightings required demotion.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked 4 corpora: official app website, full docs (including dedicated smart-contracts deployments page), GitHub repo landing page, and Plume chain contract-addresses doc. 76 addresses catalogued from the docs deployment page (live data as of 2026-09-01T09:18:44Z): 9 shared protocol contracts multi-deployed across Plume/Ethereum/BNB, 11 share tokens, 34 NestVault entrypoints, 8 EVM-side Solana bridge composer addresses, plus 3 core Plume chain tokens. Key control-surface contracts (RolesAuthority, NestShareSeizer, NestRedeemOperator) identified for downstream on-chain reads. On-chain fetch of these addresses not performed in this run (tool budget consumed); grading_basis set to 'mixed'.

protocol_metadata.about: Plume Vaults (formerly branded as Nest) is the flagship real-world asset vault protocol on Plume Network, developed by Kimber Labs Inc. Users deposit stablecoins (USDC, pUSD, USDT) into curated vaults and receive yield-bearing ERC-20 share tokens (e.g., nTBILL, nOPAL, nALPHA) representing exposure to institutional RWA strategies including US Treasuries, private credit, crypto basis trades, and payment receivables. The protocol uses an immutable three-contract architecture per vault (Core Vault, Vault Extension, Manager) with compliance enforced via a shared NestVaultPredicateProxy and RolesAuthority; vaults are accessible cross-chain via LayerZero OFT bridges to Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Solana. As of September 2026, the protocol reports over $600M in settled RWA volume across 11 active vaults with combined TVL exceeding $160M.
